subject: Request: Cross-region keystore provenance + rekey schedule (CAIQ/SIG evidence)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@northbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@northbridge.com, Procurement Team <procurement@northbridge.com>
Date: 2029-12-07T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: CAIQ/SIG evidence — cross-region keystore provenance + rekey schedule

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. As a follow-up from our SOC2/CAIQ intake, the security team needs a compact evidence bundle that covers the following for our SIG/CAIQ review: 

- Keystore provenance across regions (US-West, US-East): chain of custody for KEKs used to wrap tenant envelope keys (who created them, when, and where).
- Rekey/rotation schedule for tenant KEKs and operator actions for the last 12 months, including proof samples (signed logs or export snippets).
- HSM vendor attestation and firmware patch history for any HSMs that handled KEKs (dates and CVE references if applicable).
- Operator separation (ACLs, shift logs) and emergency rewrap/playback procedures.

Ideally we get a redacted artifact set and a short narrative (1–2 pages) describing the wrap/unwrap flow and where the cryptographic boundaries lie (Redwood control plane vs. customer BYOK). Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? We have an internal deadline of 2029-12-14 to bundle this into the CAIQ response.

I've attached the CAIQ question matrix for reference.

Thanks,

Marta Lopez
Senior InfoSec Analyst — NorthBridge Capital

Subject: Re: CAIQ/SIG evidence — cross-region keystore provenance + rekey schedule

Hi Marta,

Appreciate the clear checklist — we can assemble this. Quick plan:

- Marissa will collate the audit snapshots and the 1–2 page narrative describing our envelope encryption and cross-region wrapping model.
- Jonas will pull HSM attestations, firmware patch notes, and a redacted rotation log sample.
- Ben and I will coordinate export of the keystore inventory and confirm which items require redaction (tenant identifiers).

Target ETA: initial evidence bundle delivered to your secure share by EOD 2029-12-11, with a follow-up Q&A on 2029-12-12 if needed. Does that timing work?

One clarification request from our side: for the keystore provenance you listed "who created them" — do you need operator identity down to the individual shift log, or is a named role (e.g., "HSM Operator Team") sufficient for your CAIQ mapping?

I'll attach a short checklist of what we'll include and which files will be redacted.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-12-07T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ/SIG evidence — cross-region keystore provenance + rekey schedule

Marta / team — technical details and attachments below (summary first, artifacts attached to this thread):

Summary (short):
- Envelope encryption model: tenant data encrypted with DEKs (data keys) managed by Redwood runtime; DEKs wrapped by tenant-specific KEKs (KEK = Key Encryption Key) that reside in our HSM-backed keystore. For private/BYOK tenants, KEKs are customer-provided and ledgered.
- Cross-region provenance: KEK creation events are recorded in our keystore ledger with fields: creation_timestamp (UTC), origin_region, operator_role, wrapping_kek_id, and HSM_slot_id. We'll provide a redacted CSV extract showing the chain for the requested KEKs.
- Rotation: rotation is scheduled per tenant policy (default 90 days for managed KEKs). Rekey events include a signed operator action (JWT with operator id), HSM audit-trail pointer, and immutably-stored rewrap manifest.

Artifacts included (redacted):
1) hsm-attestation-202908.pdf — vendor attestation and FIPS module version, includes firmware ledger.
2) rotation-log-sample.txt — sample of rewrap records (timestamps and HSM pointers), personal data redacted.
3) keystore-inventory-20291207.csv — redacted provenance extract (columns: kek_id, created_at, origin_region, operator_role, hsm_slot).
4) rekey-procedures.md — short operations playbook (commands redacted where necessary).

Notes on HSM firmware history: we track firmware versions and patch notes per HSM serial. For any HSM that performed KEK generation/wrapping during the requested window we'll include the CVE-relevant notes; the vendor attestation (artifact #1) contains the signed firmware manifest for 2029-01 through 2029-11. If you need raw signed manifests for each HSM serial, let us know and we will escalate to a secure transfer.

Operator separation and shift logs: we do not publish PII. Our audit entries contain operator_role and operator_id (redacted hash). If NorthBridge requires identity-level evidence for reviewers under NDA, we can provide a hashed->clear mapping over the secure channel under an executed DPA addendum.

Technical point on cross-region key material: KEK private material never leaves HSM boundaries. When a KEK is used in a different region we perform an HSM-to-HSM remote wrap transfer (vendor-managed secure transport) and record an entry in the keystore ledger noting transport method and transport-tx-id. We'll include the ledger entries for the rows in the CSV extract.

Attachment stubs: hsm-attestation-202908.pdf (pdf, 18 pages); rotation-log-sample.txt (text, redacted); rekey-procedures.md (markdown, internal runbook, redacted).

-- Jonas Weber
Principal Applied Cryptographer — Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@northbridge.com>

The ETA of 2029-12-11 works for us. Please go ahead and prepare the redacted set; we'll confirm the NDA/secure transfer details if the reviewer requests de-anonymized mapping.

Can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on 2029-12-12 at 10:00 AM PT to run through the artifacts? If that time is not possible let me know two alternatives.

Thanks again — looking forward to the bundle.

Marta
Senior InfoSec Analyst — NorthBridge Capital
